summary: the file is not JSON the reader can follow, or its top level is neither an object nor a list, so nothing in it was read
fix: Write the file as one EPCISDocument in JSON, with the events in epcisBody.eventList, or as a JSON list of events (docs/inputs.md); fix the line named.

summary: a field the file needs is not there: the type of an event, the @context, type, schemaVersion, creationDate or epcisBody of a document, its eventList, the id of a readPoint or bizLocation, the epcClass of a quantity, the bizTransaction of a business transaction, the type and value of a source or destination, or the declarationTime of an error declaration
fix: Add the field named; docs/inputs.md lists what each part of the file needs.

summary: a key the tool does not read in that place, often a misspelt one or the field of another event type; its value was left out of every check. A key with a colon is an extension and is left alone
fix: Correct the spelling to a field of docs/inputs.md, move the field to the event type it belongs to, or name an extension field with a prefix such as example:field.

summary: a value of the wrong type or form: text where a list or an object belongs, a quantity written as text, an identifier that is not a URI, a document type or schema version the tool does not know, or a creationDate that is not a date and time with a zone
fix: Write the value as docs/inputs.md shows: text for times, identifiers and vocabulary values, lists for the lists of EPCs and quantities, objects for locations, and JSON numbers for quantities.

summary: one EPC listed twice in the same list of one event
fix: List each EPC once in each list.

summary: the file holds a private key, a seed or a mnemonic, under a key named for one or as a value shaped like one; the tool never reads it and never shows it
fix: Remove the value from the file and from wherever the file was copied, treat it as exposed and move what it controls to a new key. An event names objects, places and transactions, never the key of a ledger account.

summary: the type of an event is a word that is not one of the five event types of EPCIS 2.0; a type named by a URI is an extension and is only noted
fix: Write ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransactionEvent, TransformationEvent or AssociationEvent, with that spelling and case.

summary: an event has no eventTime, the field EPCIS calls mandatory in every event
fix: Add the eventTime: the date, time and time zone at which the event took place.

summary: an eventTime, recordTime or declarationTime that is not a date and time with a time zone, or names a day, hour or zone that does not exist
fix: Write the time as YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss, with an optional fraction of a second, and end it with Z or an offset such as +01:00.

summary: an event has no eventTimeZoneOffset, which the JSON schema requires next to the eventTime
fix: Add the eventTimeZoneOffset in effect where the event took place, such as +01:00, even when the eventTime is written in UTC.

summary: an eventTimeZoneOffset that is not a sign, two digits of hours from 00 to 14, a colon and two digits of minutes, or that has minutes with 14 hours
fix: Write the offset as +hh:mm or -hh:mm, such as +05:30 or -08:00; write Z as +00:00.

summary: an ObjectEvent, AggregationEvent, TransactionEvent or AssociationEvent has no action
fix: Add the action: ADD when the objects or the link are created, OBSERVE when they are seen unchanged, DELETE when they end.

summary: an action that is not ADD, OBSERVE or DELETE, written in capitals
fix: Write ADD, OBSERVE or DELETE, in capitals; EPCIS allows no other value.

summary: a TransformationEvent has an action, a field its type does not have
fix: Remove the action; a TransformationEvent says what was used and what was made through its inputs and outputs.

summary: an event does not name its objects as EPCIS asks: an ObjectEvent or TransactionEvent with no EPC and no quantity, an AggregationEvent or AssociationEvent with no child unless it removes them all, one with action ADD or DELETE and no parentID, or a TransactionEvent with no business transaction
fix: Name the objects in the lists of the event type, the parent of an aggregation or association that is added or removed, and the business transaction of a TransactionEvent.

summary: a TransformationEvent with no transformationID lacks inputs or outputs, or one with a transformationID has neither
fix: List what was used in inputEPCList or inputQuantityList and what was made in outputEPCList or outputQuantityList, or link events of one process with a transformationID.

summary: a quantity of 0 or below, a count that is not a whole number with no unit of measure, a unit of measure with no quantity, or a unit that is not a code of two or three capitals and digits
fix: Write a count of objects as a positive whole number with no uom, or a measure as a positive number with its UN/CEFACT code, such as KGM; leave the uom out when the quantity is unknown.

summary: an event has neither a readPoint nor a bizLocation, so no one can tell where it took place
fix: Add the readPoint where the event was seen, and the bizLocation where the objects are afterwards when they stay there.
own: asking for a readPoint or a bizLocation is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the standards it cites; EPCIS makes both optional, but an event with neither cannot be placed on a map of the chain

summary: an event has no bizStep, though the CBV says that each event should carry one
fix: Add the bizStep of the business process, such as shipping, receiving or commissioning.

summary: a bizStep that is not a business step of the CBV, alone or after a prefix of the CBV; a URI of another vocabulary is left alone
fix: Use a value of the CBV table, in lower case with underscores, such as shipping; name a step of your own with a URI of your own domain.

summary: a disposition or persistent disposition that is not a disposition of the CBV, or is one the CBV deprecates; a URI of another vocabulary is left alone
fix: Use a value of the CBV table, such as in_transit or sellable_accessible, or the value that replaces a deprecated one.

summary: two events of the file have the same eventID, and neither is an error declaration
fix: Give every event an eventID of its own, such as a UUID URI; an error declaration keeps the eventID of the event it corrects.

summary: an event has no eventID, so a ledger cannot tell the same event sent twice from two events; a note
fix: Give each event an eventID, such as a UUID URI or the hash ID of the CBV, when the events go to a ledger.
own: asking for an eventID is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the standards it cites; EPCIS makes it optional, but a shared ledger needs it to keep an event that is sent again from being written twice, so it is a note

summary: a recordTime earlier than its eventTime, or an event listed after another event of the same EPC but with an earlier eventTime
fix: Check the clocks of the readers and the order the events were captured in; list the events of an object in the order they took place.
own: comparing the times this way is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the standards it cites; EPCIS does not ask for events in time order, but a ledger that keeps them in the order they arrive shows the history of an object out of order

summary: an eventTime or recordTime later than the moment given with --now; without --now the check does not run
fix: Correct the clock or the time zone of the system that wrote the event; an event cannot take place after it is reported.
own: refusing an event from the future is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the standards it cites; EPCIS sets no rule about it, and the tool reads no clock, so the moment is the one given with --now

summary: an EPC that appears in an event later than an ObjectEvent with action DELETE, or than an event of the business step decommissioning or destroying, that named it
fix: Check whether the later event read the wrong tag or the delete was a mistake; correct the wrong event with an error declaration rather than a new event.

summary: an EPC shipped from a place it was never seen at before, while earlier events put it elsewhere, or that is received at that place only after it was shipped from there
fix: Check the readPoint and source of the shipping event and whether an event of the arrival is missing or out of place.
own: following an EPC from place to place is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the standards it cites; EPCIS says what each event means but sets no rule across events, and a file may hold only part of the history of an object

summary: a child EPC added to or observed in one parent while an earlier AggregationEvent put it in another parent and no event took it out
fix: Add the AggregationEvent with action DELETE that took the child out of its first parent, or correct the parent of the later event.
own: following the aggregations of a child is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the standards it cites; EPCIS describes each AggregationEvent on its own, and a file may not hold the event that took the child out

summary: an SGTIN, SSCC, SGLN, LGTIN or SGTIN pattern URI whose company prefix and reference do not add up to the digits of its scheme, or with a serial, lot or extension it does not allow, or a GS1 Digital Link URI with a key of the wrong length
fix: Write the EPC as the Tag Data Standard does: urn:epc:id:sgtin: with 13 digits before the serial, urn:epc:id:sscc: with 17 digits, urn:epc:id:sgln: with 12 digits before the extension.

summary: a GTIN in a GS1 Digital Link URI whose last digit is not its check digit
fix: Work the check digit out again from the other digits, or copy the GTIN again from its source.

summary: an SSCC in a GS1 Digital Link URI whose last digit is not its check digit
fix: Work the check digit out again from the first 17 digits, or copy the SSCC again from the label.

summary: a GLN in a GS1 Digital Link URI whose last digit is not its check digit
fix: Work the check digit out again from the first 12 digits, or copy the GLN again from the master data of the location.
